have been detected in the human body (liver, lung, breast, cervix, skin, adipose, and ocular tissues), and only 6 of them (a-carotene,
b-carotene, b-cryptoxanthin, lutein, zeaxanthin, and lycopene) are mainly detected in human plasma. Some carotenoids are precur-
sors of vitamin A, an essential nutrient. Other carotenoids and their metabolites provide desirable health beneﬁts to reduce the risk
of the development of chronic diseases such as eye and skin disease, type II diabetes, coronary artery disease, cancer, etc., linked to
their antioxidant nature and their ability to dissipate energy from light and free radical-generating reactions.
